title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 16
statement: A sequence \(a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots\) of positive reals satisfies \(a_{n+1}=\sqrt{\frac{1+a_{n}}{2}}\). Determine all \(a_{1}\) such that \(a_{i}=\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\) for some positive integer \(i\).

solutions.text:
Clearly \(a_{1}<1\), or else \(1 \leq a_{1} \leq a_{2} \leq a_{3} \leq \ldots\) We can therefore write \(a_{1}=\cos \theta\) for some \(0<\theta<90^{\circ}\). Note that \(\cos \frac{\theta}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos \theta}{2}}\), and \(\cos 15^{\circ}=\)
\(\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\). Hence, the possibilities for \(a_{1}\) are \(\cos 15^{\circ}, \cos 30^{\circ}\), and \(\cos 60^{\circ}\), which are \(\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), and \(\frac{1}{2}\).
